headline: Approved a ferry terminal extension at 10 Blaney Street and a rear addition at 21 Warren Street, among other home projects; continued 8 Briggs Street.
summary: Seven petitions were approved, including home additions, a conversion to three units, and extensions for 10 Blaney Street and 21 Webb Street. The 14 Gallows Hill Road variance passed 4-1. The 8 Briggs Street petition was continued to August 19, 2026.
decisions: Approved special permit for 21 Warren Street to construct a two-story rear addition, with conditions, 5-0.
Approved special permit for 46 Chestnut Street to reconstruct a rear porch and staircase, with conditions, 5-0.
Approved finding for 15 Willow Avenue to reconstruct a garage into a 2.5-story accessory dwelling unit, with conditions, 5-0.
Approved variance and special permit for 15 Abbott Street to change a two-family use to a three-family use and add a third-floor dormer, with conditions, 5-0.
Approved variance for 14 Gallows Hill Road to construct a one-story addition creating a 3.5-story house, with conditions, 4-1 (Peter Habib opposed).
Continued the petition for 8 Briggs Street to the August 19, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the minutes of the June 17, 2026 meeting as drafted.
Approved a two-year extension for the Salem Port Authority at 10 Blaney Street to exercise rights for a ferry terminal building, 5-0.
Approved a one-year extension for 21 Webb Street LLC to exercise rights for a bed and breakfast until January 28, 2027, 5-0.

City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
Meeting Minutes 
July 29, 2026 
 
A special meeting of the Salem Zoning Board of Appeals (“Salem ZBA”) was held on Wednesday, 
July 29, 2026 at 6:30 pm via remote participation in accordance with Section 30A of Chapter 20 of the Acts of 
2021, as amended by Section 40 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023, and further amended by Section 1 of Chapter 
2 of the Acts of 2025, the City is authorized to conduct remote meetings of its public bodies through June 30, 
2027.  
 
Acting Chair Christa McGaha calls the meeting to order at 6:31 pm. 
Acting Chair McGaha explains how individuals can participate in the meeting remotely via Zoom, 
and that instructions to participate remotely can also be found on the Salem website.  Ms. McGaha 
also explains the rules regarding public comment. 
 
ROLL CALL  
Those present were: Vice Chair Christa McGaha, Ellen Simpson, Peter Habib, Elena Eimert, 
Stephen Larrick, and Hilary Forbes.  Also in attendance were Brennan Postich — Staff Planner, and 
Voula Orfanos — Building Commissioner.  Those absent were: Chair Nina Vyedin 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION   
 
Pursuant to M.G.L. Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(3) to discuss strategy relating to pending litigation 
known as Roblero V. Viccica, Massachusetts Land Court, Case No. 24 MISC 000623, if the Chair 
declares that discussing the matter in an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the litigating 
position of the Board. A vote regarding whether to go into executive session is expected; and votes 
may occur during the executive session. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha explains that the public meeting will resume after the executive session 
concludes, and takes a roll call vote to enter into executive session. 
 
Roll Call Vote to Enter Executive Session:  The vote is five (5) in favor and none (0) opposed.  
The motion passes.  Executive session begins at 6:35pm. 
 
Roll Call Vote to end Executive Session:  The vote is five (5) in favor and none (0) opposed.  The 
motion passes.  Executive session ends at 7:11pm and the public meeting resumes.

Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of ARSEN SHERAJ at 15

1,200 square feet, where 15,000 square feet per dwelling unit is required. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped June 17, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Bill Quinn introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and explains that in January 2025 
the proposal was approved by the ZBA, but unfortunately changes in economic situations prevented 
the owner from executing the work within a year of the decision.  The petitioner was informed he 
would have to reapply and go before the Board of Appeals hearing process again.  Mr. Quinn 
explains the proposal is the same as that which received approval from the Board in 2025.  He 
describes the property and explains the proposal, as well as the relief being sought.  Photographs of 
the property are presented, as well as a plot plan and elevations showing existing conditions and 
proposed conditions with the new dormer.  Mr. Quinn states there has been no opposition to the 
proposal to date that he is aware of.  He describes the parking and general neighborhood conditions.

Mr. Quinn also discusses the updated variance criteria, and explains how the petition meets the 
requirements for both a special permit and a variance. 
 
Ms. Simpson indicates she recalls the petition when it previously came before the Board and that she 
does not have concerns.  Mr. Larrick and other Board members agree. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha notes one public comment was submitted, and opens the floor to public 
comment. 
 
Suzanne (no last name or address provided) states she was against the proposal the first time it was 
approved because of parking concerns.  She expresses concerns about a third family moving into the 
building, and contends that the existing two tenants/families are living in poor conditions.  She also 
states the home has been in disrepair.  Suzanne reiterates her concerns regarding parking, and argues 
that this is a neighborhood and not meant to house many people.  She states her fence fell over 
during winter because her neighbors had to shovel snow onto it and suggests this is evidence of 
density and space concerns.  She also states that the third-floor dormer will be an eyesore and that 
she will be bothered by the additional lights shining. 
 
The Board asks clarifying questions and further discusses the proposal.

Location: 14 Gallows Hill Road (Map 15, Lot 0019) (R1 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Charles Barton 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of CHARLES BARTON at 
14 GALLOWS HILL ROAD (Map 15, Lot 0019) (R1 Zoning District) for a Variance 
per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to 
construct a one-story addition to an existing 2.5-story, single-family house, creating a 
3.5-story house. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
• Application date-stamped June 30, 2026, and supporting documentation 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition. 
Charles Barton introduces himself as the owner of 14 Gallows Hill Road and explains that the 
property used to belong to his wife’s grandmother, and there is a desire to keep the home in the 
family.  Mr. Barton explains the need to increase the space for family requirements, including taking 
care of his wife’s elderly mother once she can no longer live alone.  He explains the proposal to add 
an additional story to the home, and notes that the home is assessed as a single-story house but that 
the planning department considers it a two-story house, and so relief is required as the addition 
makes it a three-story home.  He presents elevations of proposed conditions and explains the relief 
being requested further.  Mr. Barton also presents photographs of similar homes in the 
neighborhood that have had the same types of additions, and suggests it is in line with 
neighborhood characteristics.  A plot plan is presented showing existing and proposed conditions.   
 
The Board members ask clarifying questions.  Mr. Habib states he does not feel the proposal is in 
line with neighborhood characteristics and that he believes the proposed addition to be oversized.  
Mr. Barton explains there are other homes in Witchcraft Heights that are similar to what is being 
proposed, and Mr. Habib suggests those properties are also too large for the space and setting.  Mr. 
Barton also notes that the variance is for the number of stories, as the home meets the actual height 
restrictions in feet.  Ms. Simpson acknowledges there are other homes in the neighborhood the size 
of the proposal, but agrees with Mr. Habib that they seem large for the area.  She states she is not
